mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, and TRANSIT mobility over the last four weeks indicates a broad and sustained return to pre-pandemic activity levels, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, falling below 12% above baseline for two consecutive weeks, signifies a population shift towards spending more time outside the home, directly translating to increased foot traffic and higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 12% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase relative to the previous 14 days, despite RESIDENTIAL falling below 12% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined upward trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a strong return to daily commuting and office presence. This synergistic effect will drive increased weekday spending and leisure activities, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue their upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant and sustained increase in PARKS mobility, coinciding with the late winter/early spring period, suggests improving weather conditions are encouraging outdoor activities. This seasonal shift will extend to general leisure and shopping, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility, a proxy for essential movement, shows a week-on-week decline of more than 2 points, it signals a potential tightening of public health restrictions or increased caution, which would negatively impact discretionary retail and lead to lower RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines by more than 2 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC increases over the subsequent 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent positive momentum in RETAIL_REC itself, showing a clear trend of becoming less negative over the past four weeks, indicates an inherent recovery trajectory that will persist, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite the prior four-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous strong increase in PARKS mobility and a decrease in RESIDENTIAL time indicates a significant shift in public behavior towards outdoor and out-of-home activities. This combined behavioral change will directly translate to increased engagement with retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility, despite recent gains, fails to recover significantly and remains above -20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks, it indicates a persistent remote work policy or lack of office return, which will continue to suppress weekday retail activity, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains above -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -20% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases compared to the last 28 days.
